data_rows: rolling 30 s window; ~91 samples per series at the moment captured (3 series)

model.rules: Reynolds separation + alignment + cohesion (no predator, no leader)
model.sweep: three independent runs, same seed-7 start, w_align in {0.3, 1.0, 2.0}, sep 1.5 / coh 1.0 held
model.integration: fixed-rate setInterval (~33 Hz step, ~6 Hz re-render); step sequence identical to D3/p5

gotchas_hit: Plot's UMD bundle (dist/plot.umd.min.js) EXTERNALISES d3 — it expects window.d3 to already exist. Loading only the Plot script leaves window.Plot = {} (the UMD factory throws on the missing d3 dependency, and the throw does NOT surface in the console). Symptom downstream: 'Plot.frame is not a function'. Fix: load d3@7 BEFORE the Plot script.

Plot has no native animation: the model is stepped on a setInterval and Plot re-renders the whole figure on a slow tick via replaceChildren(Plot.plot(...)). For a slow analytical view this is the right shape; a fixed-rate timer also dodges the background-tab rAF-throttle that bites the 60 fps Specimens.
Faceted small-multiples need an explicit shared y-domain (y: {domain: [0,1]}) so the three R curves are visually comparable; without it each facet auto-scales and the comparison lies.
Histogram x-domain must be set from the live max neighbor count, else empty high bins clip or the axis jumps frame-to-frame.

verification.method: static server + headless eval/screenshot; stepOnce() pumped 900x then draw() (setInterval throttled in background tab)

notes: Final R-by-alignment matches the Node reference for the identical model to 3 decimals — confirms the in-browser sims run the same deterministic trajectory as the other two Specimens. This is the brief that earns grammar-of-graphics its keep: three small multiples from essentially one Plot.plot() call via fx faceting. The grammar's beautiful defaults read visibly different from D3/p5 — that difference is part of what the Comparison reveals.
